article.title: The yield curve un-inverted. Now what?
article.lede: The 2s/10s spread closed positive for a third consecutive session — the cleanest signal we've had since August 2022. The reflex is to call it a recession all-clear. It is not.

body.text: The standard playbook says a steepener after a long inversion is the bell for a recession that has already arrived. The cleaner reading — and the one we've been running on the desk since March — is that the bull steepener of the past two weeks is policy-driven, not growth-driven. The front end is moving on a Fed that finally has cover; the long end is sitting where it was in February.

First, IG credit spreads. The OAS on the LQD basket has widened 14bps off the early-April tights, but is still 38bps below its 5-year average. Real money is not behaving like the curve. That tension resolves one of two ways and historically the spread market gets the answer first.

Second, the dollar. DXY is range-bound between 102 and 104, and the cross-asset volatility in CNY has fallen to a 14-month low. A clean steepener with a soft dollar is the policy-driven outcome. A steepener with a strong dollar would mean something else, and we are not seeing it.

transcript.title: Transcript preview
transcript.sub: First five minutes. Full transcript and search for Pro Desk members.

lines.text: Welcome back. We're recording on the morning of May 14, the 2s/10s spread closed positive for the third session, and the question on the desk this morning is the same question that's in every chat in the open finance world: is it over.

It's not over. And the reason it's not over is the same reason we've been talking about it for six weeks — the steepener is policy-driven, the long end isn't moving, and credit spreads are not behaving like the curve.
Let me push back on that for a second. We had a strong CPI print, the Fed dot plot drifted, the front end ripped — that's a real steepener. Why is that different from a 1995 cycle steepener?

Two reasons. One: in 1995 you also had the long end coming in — soft landing, term premium compression, the whole thing. This time the long end is essentially where it was in February. Two: the dollar.

about.title: A small editorial house, run by people who read both tapes.
about.lede: We are not a guru, not a day-trading service, not an aggregator. We are a small editorial house built on the belief that the next decade of investing requires reading two markets in two languages, with the same standards.
method: Every dated call carries a source, a date, and the criteria that would change our mind. We publish our misses with the same prominence as our hits.
We do not take advertising or sponsorship. We do not run hidden affiliate links. Subscription revenue is our only revenue.
We do not publish before 07:00 ET on issue days — period. No 'breaking' email at 02:00 to be first to wrong.
coi: Editors disclose personal holdings on any single-name call, dated to the issue.
Editors do not trade the names they cover on the day of publication, or the day after.
The full COI policy lives on the methodology page. [CTO TO PROVIDE final wording before launch.]
